02. The facts in brief of the petitioner's case is that:
On 12.01.2022 at about 08.00 a.m. the deceased Mustafa Sayyad @ Syed Mustafa was pillion rider of the new unregistered bike ridden by his friend Shivakumar and when they reach near R.K. As a result he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed on the spot.

Soon after the accident, he was shifted to Government hospital, Hiriyur, wherein,
after the postmortem, body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body and for performing obsequies ceremonies.
It is further stated in the petition that, prior to the accident deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 27 years and was working as AC Mechanic, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are suffering from mental shock, financial loss and mental agony.
It is further stated, that the accident was occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the litter/Garbage disposal vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-16-C- 6113.
The jurisdictional police have registered a case against the driver of the litter/Garbage disposal vehicle U/Sec. 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The 1 st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle at the time of accident are liable to pay compensation.
03. On service of summons, Respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the court and filed written statements.
04. The Respondent No.1 in his written statement stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts, and the same is liable to be dismissed.

This respondent has denied the age,
occupation and income of the deceased and also the entire averments of the claim petition.

Further stated that there is no negligence on the part of driver of the offending litter/Garbage disposal vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-C-6113 and the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the unregisterd bike.
It is further contended that the driver of the lorry was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
The offending lorry is not duly insured with the 1 st respondent and if at all policy is issued, liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Among other ground prays for dismissal of the petition.

05. The 2nd respondent in his objection statement has contended that no claim is maintainable against an Unregistered vehicle which is not supposed to be driven on road without registration and without insurance and hence seller alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The vendor of the unregistered bike is not made as a party and hence petition is not maintainable and the same is deserves to be allowed.
He also denied other averments of the petitioner and among other grounds prayed for dismissal of the petition.
06. On the basis of above pleadings, the issues were framed by my predecessor in the office, which are recasted

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioners prove that on 12.01.2022 at about 08.00 a.m. the deceased Mustafa Sayyad @ Syed Mustafa was pillion rider of the new unregistered bike ridden by his friend Shivakumar and when they reach near R.K. Powergen, Hiriyr Taluk,
Chitradurga, at that time, the driver of the litter/Garbage disposal vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-16-C-6113 drove the same in a rash and negligent and zigzag manner and took sudden right turn and dashed against the bike on which the deceased was proceeding.
As a result he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed on the spot.
2. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
07. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, the 1st petitioner got examined herself as PW-1 and produced 20 documents which are marked as Ex.P1 to 20 and closed their side of evidence.
On the other hand, respondents have not led their defence evidence.
08. Heard arguments on both the sides.

In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following;
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1: The claim of the petitioners is that, On 12.01.2022 at about 08.00 a.m. the deceased Mustafa Sayyad @ Syed Mustafa was pillion rider of the new unregistered bike ridden by his friend Shivakumar and when they reach near R.K. Powergen, Hiriyur Taluk, Chitradurga, at that time, the driver of the litter/Garbage disposal vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-16-C-6113 drove the same in a rash and negligent and zigzag manner and took sudden right turn and dashed against the bike on which the deceased was proceeding.
As a result he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed on the spot.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Government hospital, Hiriyur, wherein after the postmortem, body was handed over to the petitioners and they performed funeral and obsequies by spending huge amount.
11. The petitioners in order to prove the above said fact, examined the 1st petitioner as PW.1 by filing his affidavit, which is in consonance with the petition averments.

She has produced 20 documents,
which were marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P20.

Ex.P1 is the true copy of the F.I.R, Ex.P2 is the true copy of First information statement, Ex.P3 is the true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4 is the true copy of vehicle release mahazar, Ex.P5 is the true copy of sketch, Ex.P6 is the true copy of IMV report, Ex.P7 and 8 K.T. 12.
The death of Syed Mustafa is not disputed.

The PM report as well as other relevant documents establishes that the Syed Mustafa died in road traffic accident which occurred on12.01.2022 between the unregistered bike and the litter/Garbage disposal vehicle bearing No.KA-16-C- 6113.
13.
The first information was given by 1 st petitioner, who is the wife of deceased on 12.01.2022.
On the basis of the first information, the police attached to the Hiriyur PS registered FIR on 12.01.2022 itself for the offences punishable U/Sec 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
On perusal of Ex.P11 charge sheet, the Investigating Officer after investigation filed the charge sheet against the driver of the litter/Garbage disposal vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-16-C- 6113.

In Para No.17 of the charge sheet it is stated that the driver of the litter/Garbage disposal vehicle came from Yadiyur-Tiptur road, Hegadarahalli, Belagarahalli, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased, due to which the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to death on the spot.
14. The PW-1 is cross examined by the learned counsel for respondents.
The PW-1 is not an eye witness to the alleged accident.
She gave first information based on the information received by her from others regarding the accident.
It is suggested to her that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motor bike by its rider which is denied by her.

It is also suggested that the deceased fell down from the bike and the driver of the Garbage vehicle was falsely implicated to get compensation which is also denied by the PW-1, as stated above the PW-1 is not an eye witness to the alleged accident.

If the deceased fell down from the bike and the driver of the Garbage vehicle was falsely implicated in the first information then why the I.O. filed charge sheet against the driver of the Garbage vehicle is not explained by the respondents.
We have the reply given by the commissioner, Town municipal, Hiriyur marked as Ex.P8 wherein he admits the collusion of two vehicles and the accident.
He took possession of the Garbage vehicle from the custody of the police negative the say of the respondents hence, counsel that the deceased himself fell down from the bike.
The respondent No.2 has not denied the alleged accident in his written statement.
From this it is very clear that the deceased died in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar and Ex.P5 is the sketch.
On perusal of the sketch the accident was occurred in the middle of the road.
The Garbage dumping yard is shown on the eastern side of the road which runs from south to north.
The Hiriyur is situated on the south.
The driver of the Garbage vehicle after collecting the Garbage in the Hiriyur Town proceed towards Challakere and took the vehicle to the right side to dump the Garbage in the garbage Yard.
While doing so the driver without seeing the vehicles which are flying on the road took the vehicle to the right side and as such he hit against the motor bike.

As such the pillion rider sustained injuries and K.T. Ramesh vs Sompalam Hussain Basha on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104869244/
5 died in the spot.

sentences.text: If the driver of the Garbage vehicle stopped his vehicle and after observing the vehicles which are flying on the road and took to right side then he could have avoid the accident.
Since he took his vehicle to the right side he hit the motor bike.
Hence, there is negligence on the part of the driver of Garbage vehicle.
The learned counsel for respondent argued that the vehicle is not registered and as such the petitioners are not entitled for compensation.
If the vehicle is not registered and if it fly on the road then it is an offence under M.V. Act, but that does not mean that the driver of any other vehicle can hit the unregistered vehicle.
The P.M. report marked as Ex.P10 demonstrate that the deceased died due to injuries and shock due to hemorrhage as a result of road traffic accident.
Ex.P6 IMV report indicates that the accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicles.
Hence, the petitioners able to prove that the husband of the 1st petitioner died in road traffic accident and the driver of the vehicle bearing No.KA-16-C- 6113 is responsible for the accident.
Accordingly, I answered issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2 and 3:
The petitioners claimed that, they are the legal heir of deceased Mustafa Sayyad @ Syed Mustafa.

The petitioners in order to prove that, they are the legal heirs have produced the Ex.P12, Ex.P16 to 19 Aadhar card of deceased, adhaar card of 1 st petitioner, birth certificate of 2nd petitioner, adhaar cards of 2 nd petitioner and 3rd petitioner.
On perusal of the said documents, it goes to show that, petitioners are the wife, child and mother of deceased Mustafa Sayyad @ Syed Mustafa.
Hence they are entitled for compensation.
16. Loss of Dependency / Loss of estate: The Ex.P12 is the Adhaar and Ex.P20 is the birth certificate of deceased Mustafa Sayyad @ Syed Mustafa.
On perusal of the said documents goes to show that the date of birth of deceased is 18.04.1994.
Accident was occurred on 12.01.2022.
Hence on the date of accident the age of deceased was 27 years 09 months.
17. The Postmortem report, inquest, Charge sheet reveals that the cause of death of deceased is due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
Hence the petitioners being the legal heirs are entitled for compensation.
The petitioners are wife, child and mother of deceased and they are the legal heirs of the deceased and they are dependents of the deceased.
18. As per petition averments, the deceased was a AC mechanic and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
There is no evidence before the Tribunal that he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The Ex.P15 the National Trade certificate issued by the Member Secretary, NCFVI, goes to show that the deceased passed prescribed trade test in the trade of electrician.
Hence he is a skilled labour.
Now a days the agricultural labourer or coolie earns Rs.500/- per day.
The accident occurred in the year 2022.

Hence, the income of deceased per month is considered as Rs.15,000/- p.m.,
19.
The income of the deceased per month is Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Hence by applying the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarala Varma Vs DTC reported in AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104, 1/3rd is deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarala Varma Vs DTC reported in AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the expenditure of deceased became 1/3 x 15,000 = 5,000/- and income of deceased per month became Rs.10,000/- (15,000-5,000).
The age of the deceased at the time of accident was 27 years and hence 40% is added towards future prospectus.

Hence the income of the deceased becomes Rs.14,0000/-
p.m. (10,000+4,000)

sentences.text: The age of the deceased was 27 years at the time of accident.
Hence, the proper multiplier as per the above citation is 17.

Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.14,000x12x17=28,56,000/-
under the head of loss of dependency.
21. Love and affection and loss of consortium:
The petitioners being the wife, child and mother of deceased have lost love and affection of deceased towards them and vice versa.
No amount of compensation gives back the deceased.
Hence by considering all these the petitioners are entitled for Rs.50,000/-.
22. Funeral Expenses:
The petitioners in their petition have stated that they have spent amount towards funeral expenditure.
In order to prove the same they have not produced any documents.
However, they have incurred some amount towards funeral ceremony.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenditure.
23.
Conveyance charges:
The petitioners have not produced any documents to show that they have spent amount towards conveyance.
At the time of incident nobody received the receipt.
They hired the vehicle to shift the deceased to hospital and hospital to home town.
Hence by considering this fact the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,000/-.

24. The above amount is summarized as follows;

25.
The petitioners have claimed interest on the compensation amount.
Hence by considering the rate of interest in nationalized bank the petitioners are entitled for interest at the rate of 6%.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
26. Issue No. 4:

In view of the foregoing reasons I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/s 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is partly allowed with cost.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount and directed to deposit the above said amount within 2 months from the date of this order along with accrued interest.
The petitioners are equally entitled to receive the compensation amount.

After deposit of the compensation amount by the respondent No.1, 50% share amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of the petitioners no.1 and 3 respectively in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% share amount shall be released to them through e-payment on proper identification.

Since the petitioner No.2 is minor, his share of compensation ordered to be kept in fixed deposit till he attains the age of majority and the petitioner No.1/guardian of the minor petitioner is entitled to take periodical interest and to utilise the same for the welfare of the child.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw Award accordingly.

The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount and directed to deposit the above said amount within 2 months from the date of this order along with accrued interest.
The petitioners are equally entitled to receive the compensation amount.
After deposit of the compensation amount by the respondent No.1, 50% share amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of the petitioners no.1 and 3 respectively in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% share amount shall be released to them through e-payment on proper identification.
